reading: The empty interior of the 5-outline square is split into four 2x2 quadrants; the quadrant nearest each outside marker (diagonal to a frame corner) and its diagonally opposite quadrant are filled with that marker's colour.

slots.region: interior of the one rectangular outline (frame)
slots.markers: two single cells outside the frame, each diagonal to a frame corner
slots.pattern: 2x2 quadrant checker: marker colour in its own corner quadrant and the opposite quadrant

why: every interior cell takes the colour of the marker whose corner quadrant is it or its diagonal opposite; frame and markers unchanged

reading: A strip of colour columns (a key) gives a top-to-bottom colour order; copies of the repeated shape are stacked vertically in that order, keeping the existing copies in place, and the key is erased.
verb: stack shape copies in key order

slots.key: multi-row strip whose columns read left-to-right give the colour order
slots.unit: the shape shared by the existing coloured copies
slots.placement: copies abut vertically in the same columns, extending above/below the existing ones

why: output is the shape stacked once per key colour in key order, aligned with the existing copies; key removed

reading: The four single cells in the inner corners of the outline are removed and each reappears just outside the frame at the diagonally opposite corner (point reflection through the frame centre, pushed one step out).
verb: send corner marks to opposite outer corners

slots.subject: the four marks inside the frame at its inner corners
slots.target: cell diagonally outside the opposite frame corner

why: each inner-corner mark of colour c appears at the outer diagonal of the opposite corner; interior becomes background

reading: The most common colour stays; every other cell becomes 5.
why: every non-background cell of any colour becomes 5; background (majority) cells unchanged

reading: Every 2x2 grey block gets four diagonal corner cells: 1 top-left, 2 top-right, 3 bottom-left, 4 bottom-right.
why: around each object the 4x4 pattern 1002/0550/0550/3004 appears (block plus diagonal corner cells); all else unchanged

reading: The grid of grey separator lines is redrawn clean: all noise cells in the panels are cleared, noise on lines becomes grey, and every line crossing takes the noise colour.

slots.lines: full (majority) grey separator rows and columns
slots.crossings: row-line x column-line intersections, coloured with the noise colour

why: output = separator rows/columns in 5, their intersections in the noise colour, everything else 0

reading: The output is twice as wide; the horizontally periodic band is continued with its period over the new width.
verb: extend periodic pattern to double width

slots.pattern: each row's minimal horizontal period, continued to the new width

why: out[y][x] = in[y][x mod p] for the smallest period p of the input rows, width 2W

reading: Each pair of same-coloured markers on the lattice of 3x3 rings spans a rectangle snapped outward to the gutter lines; the rectangle outline is drawn on the gutters in that colour and the centre of every ring inside it is filled with that colour.
verb: draw lattice box between marker pair

slots.markers: two cells of one colour (per colour) on the lattice
slots.box: bounding box of the pair, expanded outward to the nearest gutter rows/columns
slots.outline: box border on gutter lines in marker colour
slots.fill: centre cells of rings inside the box in marker colour

why: every gutter cell on the box border and every enclosed ring centre has the marker colour; rings and cells outside unchanged

reading: Each marker cell in the top row drops a full vertical line down its column; cells of other colours become the marker colour, cells of the marker's own colour become background.
verb: drop column lines, invert on own colour

slots.source: non-background cells of the top row
slots.colour: marker colour, except background where the cell already has the marker colour

why: in each marked column every cell below row 0 is marker colour if it was not, background if it was; other columns unchanged

reading: Two framed panels; each shape in the left panel is copied onto the same rows of the empty right panel, keeping its side alignment: left-aligned shapes stay at the left margin, right-aligned at the right margin, and full-width bars stretch across the right panel.
verb: project panel content with margin anchoring

slots.alignment: keep distance to the left or right panel edge; shapes touching both margins stretch to the new width

why: each source row's shape appears in the target panel on the same rows with the same margin to its anchored side(s)
